alabama.overview: Alabama LLCs are formed by filing a Certificate of Formation with the Alabama Secretary of State. Alabama is distinctive because you must first obtain a Certificate of Name Reservation before filing, and there is no annual report to file with the Secretary of State.
alabama.filing_office: Alabama Secretary of State — Business Services
alabama.registered_agent: Every LLC must maintain a registered agent with a physical street address in Alabama where legal papers can be delivered; the agent may be an Alabama resident or a business authorized to do business in Alabama.
alabama.operating_agreement: Recommended, not required — Alabama law defines a limited liability company agreement as written, oral or implied, and no written agreement must be filed with the state (Ala. Code 10A-5A-1.02(l))
alabama.annual_report: No annual report; $0. Alabama eliminated the annual report requirement for all business entities effective October 1, 2024 under Act 2024-213.
alabama.series_llc: Yes — Alabama authorizes series LLCs under Ala. Code 10A-5A-11.01 to 10A-5A-11.16, with separate series that can hold their own assets and liabilities if records are kept separate.
alabama.foreign_llc: An LLC formed in another state must register as a foreign LLC with the Alabama Secretary of State before doing business in Alabama; the filing fee is $150.
alabama.single_member: Single-member LLCs are allowed in Alabama and follow the same formation process as multi-member LLCs.

alaska.overview: Alaska has no Secretary of State; LLCs are formed with the Division of Corporations, Business and Professional Licensing. Alaska has one of the highest formation fees at $250, and a new LLC also needs a separate state business license before doing business.
alaska.filing_office: Alaska Division of Corporations, Business and Professional Licensing — Corporations Section
alaska.registered_agent: Every LLC must maintain a registered agent with a physical street address in Alaska, with both a physical address and a mailing address in Alaska; the agent may be an Alaska resident or a corporation authorized in Alaska, and the LLC cannot be its own agent.
alaska.operating_agreement: Recommended, not required — Alaska law addresses operating agreements in AS 10.50.095, but no operating agreement must be filed with the state.
alaska.annual_report: Biennial report (not annual): $100 every two years, due before January 2 of the filing year; a free initial report is due within 6 months of formation, and a separate Alaska business license costs $50 per year.
alaska.series_llc: No — state law does not authorize series LLCs; the Alaska LLC Act (AS 10.50) has no series provisions.
alaska.foreign_llc: An LLC formed in another state must register as a foreign LLC with the Division of Corporations on Form 08-0497; the filing fee is $350.
alaska.single_member: Single-member LLCs are allowed in Alaska and follow the same formation process as multi-member LLCs.

arizona.overview: Arizona LLCs are formed with the Arizona Corporation Commission, not the Secretary of State, for a low $50 filing fee. Arizona has no annual report, but most new LLCs must publish a notice of formation in a newspaper unless the statutory agent is in Maricopa or Pima County.
arizona.registered_agent: Every LLC must maintain a statutory agent with a physical street address in Arizona where legal papers can be delivered during business hours; the agent may be an Arizona resident or a business authorized to do business in Arizona.
arizona.operating_agreement: Recommended, not required — Arizona law allows an operating agreement to be written, oral or implied (A.R.S. 29-3105), and no operating agreement is filed with the Commission.
arizona.annual_report: No annual report; $0. Arizona LLCs file no annual or biennial report with the Corporation Commission.
arizona.series_llc: No — state law does not authorize series LLCs; the Arizona Limited Liability Company Act (A.R.S. Title 29, Chapter 7) has no series provisions.
arizona.foreign_llc: An LLC formed in another state must register as a foreign LLC with the Arizona Corporation Commission on Form L-025; the filing fee is $150 ($185 expedited).
arizona.single_member: Single-member LLCs are allowed in Arizona and follow the same formation process as multi-member LLCs.

arkansas.overview: Arkansas LLCs are formed by filing a Certificate of Organization with the Arkansas Secretary of State. Formation is inexpensive, but every LLC then owes a flat $150 franchise tax each year, which is much larger than the formation fee.
arkansas.filing_office: Arkansas Secretary of State — Business and Commercial Services Division
arkansas.registered_agent: Every LLC must maintain a registered agent with a physical street address in Arkansas, not a post office box, where legal papers can be delivered during business hours.
arkansas.operating_agreement: Recommended, not required — Arkansas law does not require an operating agreement, and no operating agreement is filed with the state.
arkansas.annual_report: Annual LLC Franchise Tax Report: $150 flat, due on or before May 1 each year, starting in the calendar year after formation.
arkansas.series_llc: Yes — Arkansas authorizes series LLCs under the Arkansas Uniform Protected Series Act, Ark. Code Ann. 4-37-101 to 4-37-805, effective October 1, 2019; each additional protected series requires a separate $50 filing.
arkansas.foreign_llc: An LLC formed in another state must register as a foreign LLC with the Arkansas Secretary of State on Form FL-01; the filing fee is $270 online / $300 by mail.
arkansas.single_member: Single-member LLCs are allowed in Arkansas and follow the same formation process as multi-member LLCs.

california.overview: California LLCs are formed by filing Articles of Organization (Form LLC-1) with the California Secretary of State for $70. The filing fee is low, but California is expensive to maintain: every LLC owes an $800 minimum annual tax to the Franchise Tax Board.
california.filing_office: California Secretary of State — Business Programs Division
california.registered_agent: Every LLC must maintain an agent for service of process with a physical street address in California where legal papers can be delivered during normal business hours.
california.operating_agreement: Required — California requires every LLC, including a single-member LLC, to have an operating agreement, whether written or oral, though it is kept with the LLC records and not filed with the state (Cal. Corp. Code 17701.01 to 17701.02).
california.annual_report: Statement of Information: $20, due within 90 days of formation and then every two years; plus an $800 minimum annual tax to the Franchise Tax Board, due by the 15th day of the 4th month after formation.
california.series_llc: No — state law does not authorize domestic series LLCs; a series LLC formed in another state may register in California, but each series is treated as a separate LLC for California tax purposes.
california.foreign_llc: An LLC formed in another state must register as a foreign LLC with the California Secretary of State on Form LLC-5; the filing fee is $70.
california.single_member: A single-member LLC is allowed in California, but it must still have an operating agreement, and it still owes the $800 minimum annual tax.

colorado.overview: Colorado LLCs are formed online only with the Colorado Secretary of State for $50, one of the lowest formation fees in the country. Ongoing compliance is also cheap, with a single yearly Periodic Report.
colorado.registered_agent: Every LLC must maintain a registered agent with a physical street address in Colorado, not a post office box; since July 1, 2025, an individual agent must verify Colorado residency with a Colorado driver license or state ID number.
colorado.operating_agreement: Recommended, not required — Colorado law does not require an operating agreement, and no operating agreement is filed with the state.
colorado.annual_report: Periodic Report: $25 per year, filed online in the window from two months before to two months after the LLC formation anniversary month.
colorado.series_llc: No — state law does not authorize series LLCs; Colorado law has no provision for creating protected series within a single LLC.
colorado.foreign_llc: An LLC formed in another state must register as a foreign LLC with the Colorado Secretary of State by filing a Statement of Foreign Entity Authority; the filing fee is $100.
colorado.single_member: Single-member LLCs are allowed in Colorado and follow the same formation process as multi-member LLCs.

connecticut.overview: Connecticut LLCs are formed by filing a Certificate of Organization with the Secretary of the State for $120. The certificate includes the appointment of the registered agent, and the LLC then files an $80 annual report each year.
connecticut.filing_office: Connecticut Secretary of the State — Business Services Division
connecticut.registered_agent: Every LLC must maintain a registered agent, called a statutory agent, with a physical street address in Connecticut where legal papers can be delivered; the agent appointment is included in the Certificate of Organization.
connecticut.operating_agreement: Recommended, not required — Connecticut law defines an operating agreement broadly to include oral, implied or written agreements (Conn. Gen. Stat. 34-243a(20)), and no operating agreement is filed with the state.
connecticut.annual_report: Annual report: $80, filed online each year between January 1 and March 31, starting in the calendar year after formation.
connecticut.series_llc: No — state law does not authorize series LLCs; the Connecticut Uniform Limited Liability Company Act (Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 613a, sections 34-243 to 34-283d) has no series provision.
connecticut.foreign_llc: An LLC formed in another state must register as a foreign LLC with the Secretary of the State by filing a Foreign Registration Statement; the filing fee is $120.
connecticut.single_member: Single-member LLCs are allowed in Connecticut and follow the same formation process as multi-member LLCs.

delaware.overview: Delaware LLCs are formed by filing a short Certificate of Formation with the Division of Corporations for $110. Delaware is popular for its flexible LLC law and privacy, but every LLC pays a flat annual tax and must keep a Delaware registered agent.
delaware.filing_office: Delaware Department of State — Division of Corporations
delaware.registered_agent: Every LLC must maintain a registered agent with a physical street address in Delaware, not a post office box, where legal papers can be delivered; the agent may be a Delaware resident or a business authorized to do business in Delaware.
delaware.operating_agreement: Recommended, not required — Delaware law is built around the LLC agreement, but it is a private internal document and is not filed with the state.
delaware.annual_report: No annual report; $400 annual LLC tax due June 1 each year, for tax year 2026 onward.
delaware.series_llc: Yes — Delaware authorizes series LLCs under 6 Del. C. 18-215; a series may hold assets, enter contracts, and sue or be sued in its own name, and each registered series owes an additional $100 annual tax.
delaware.foreign_llc: An LLC formed in another state must register as a foreign LLC with the Division of Corporations by filing a Certificate of Registration, with a certificate of existence from its home state dated within 6 months; the filing fee is $200, plus the $400 annual tax.
delaware.single_member: Single-member LLCs are allowed in Delaware and follow the same formation process as multi-member LLCs.

florida.overview: Florida LLCs are formed by filing Articles of Organization with the Division of Corporations through Sunbiz for $125 total. Florida has no state personal income tax, but its $138.75 annual report is higher than the formation fee and carries a $400 late penalty after May 1.
florida.filing_fee: $125 ($100 for the Articles of Organization plus $25 for the registered agent designation)
florida.filing_office: Florida Department of State — Division of Corporations (Sunbiz)
florida.registered_agent: Every LLC must continuously maintain a registered agent with a physical street address in Florida, not a post office box, who is available during business hours to accept service of process; the agent must sign a written acceptance.
florida.operating_agreement: Recommended, not required — Florida law allows an operating agreement to be oral, implied, in a record, or any combination (Fla. Stat. 605.0102), and no operating agreement is filed with the state.
florida.annual_report: Annual report: $138.75, due between January 1 and May 1 each year, starting in the calendar year after formation; a $400 late fee applies after May 1.
florida.series_llc: Yes — Florida authorizes protected series LLCs under Fla. Stat. 605.2101 to 605.2802, the Uniform Protected Series Provisions, effective July 1, 2026; an existing Florida LLC designates a protected series online for $25 per series.
florida.foreign_llc: An LLC formed in another state must register as a foreign LLC with the Division of Corporations; the filing fee is $125 ($100 plus $25 for the registered agent designation).
florida.single_member: Single-member LLCs are allowed in Florida and follow the same formation process as multi-member LLCs.

georgia.overview: Georgia LLCs are formed by filing Articles of Organization with the Secretary of State Corporations Division. Formation is inexpensive, and the only recurring state filing is a $60 Annual Registration due each spring.
georgia.filing_fee: $110 ($100 filing fee plus $10 service charge, online or by mail)
georgia.filing_office: Georgia Secretary of State — Corporations Division
georgia.registered_agent: Every LLC must continuously maintain a registered agent with a physical street address in Georgia, not a post office box, who is available during business hours to accept legal papers (O.C.G.A. 14-11-209).
georgia.operating_agreement: Recommended, not required — Georgia law does not require an operating agreement, and no operating agreement is filed with the state.
georgia.annual_report: Annual Registration: $60 ($50 plus $10 service charge), due each year between January 1 and April 1, starting in the calendar year after formation.
georgia.series_llc: No — state law does not authorize series LLCs; the Georgia Limited Liability Company Act (O.C.G.A. Title 14, Chapter 11) has no series provision.
georgia.foreign_llc: An LLC formed in another state must register as a foreign LLC with the Corporations Division by filing an Application for Certificate of Authority (Form CD 241); the filing fee is $235 ($225 plus $10 service charge).
georgia.single_member: Single-member LLCs are allowed in Georgia and follow the same formation process as multi-member LLCs.

hawaii.overview: Hawaii has no Secretary of State for business filings; LLCs file with the Department of Commerce and Consumer Affairs, Business Registration Division. The filing fee is low at $51 total. Annual reports follow an unusual quarterly schedule tied to the calendar quarter in which the LLC registered.
hawaii.filing_fee: $51 total ($50 filing fee plus $1 State Archives fee)
hawaii.filing_office: Hawaii Department of Commerce and Consumer Affairs — Business Registration Division
hawaii.registered_agent: Every LLC must continuously maintain a registered agent with a business address in Hawaii; the agent may be a Hawaii resident individual or a domestic or foreign entity authorized to do business in Hawaii (HRS section 428-107).
hawaii.operating_agreement: recommended, not required (HRS section 428-103 permits an operating agreement; it is not filed with the DCCA)
hawaii.annual_report: Annual report due each year by the end of the calendar quarter in which the LLC registered (March 31, June 30, September 30 or December 31), starting the year after formation; $12.50 online / $15 on paper
hawaii.foreign_llc: A foreign LLC must file an Application for Certificate of Authority (Form FLLC-1) with the DCCA before transacting business in Hawaii; $50 plus $1 State Archives fee

idaho.overview: Idaho LLCs are formed by filing a Certificate of Organization with the Secretary of State, online through SOSBiz or on paper. Filing costs $100 online, and the required annual report is free, making Idaho one of the cheapest states to maintain an LLC in.
idaho.filing_fee: $100 online / $120 by mail or in person ($100 plus $20 manual processing fee)
idaho.registered_agent: The registered agent must be an Idaho resident individual or a business entity authorized in Idaho, with a physical Idaho street address (no P.O. box), available during normal business hours (Idaho Code section 30-21-403).
idaho.operating_agreement: recommended, not required (Idaho Code sections 30-25-102(9) and 30-25-201(c); the agreement may be oral, implied or written and is not filed with the Secretary of State)
idaho.annual_report: Annual report due each year by the last day of the LLC's formation month, starting the year after formation; $0 (no fee)
idaho.foreign_llc: A foreign LLC must file a foreign registration statement with the Idaho Secretary of State before transacting business in Idaho. A foreign LLC must file a foreign registration statement with the Idaho Secretary of State before transacting business in Idaho; the fee is $100 online ($120 on paper, which adds a $20 manual-processing fee).
idaho.single_member: One person can form an Idaho LLC; the operating agreement is the agreement of all the members, including a sole member, and may be oral, implied or written (Idaho Code section 30-25-102).

illinois.overview: Illinois LLCs file Articles of Organization (Form LLC-5.5) with the Secretary of State, Department of Business Services, for $150. Illinois is one of the states that authorizes series LLCs, at a higher $400 filing fee. There is no newspaper publication requirement.
illinois.filing_fee: $150 ($400 for an LLC with the power to establish series)
illinois.filing_office: Illinois Secretary of State, Department of Business Services
illinois.registered_agent: The LLC must have a registered agent with an Illinois street address (registered office in Illinois) who can accept legal papers on behalf of the LLC.
illinois.operating_agreement: recommended, not required (805 ILCS 180/1-5 and 180/15-5; the agreement may be oral, in a record, implied or any combination, and is not filed with the state)
illinois.annual_report: Annual report (Form LLC-50.1) due each year within the 60 days before the first day of the LLC's anniversary month; $75 (plus $50 for each series with a certificate of designation)
illinois.series_llc: Yes — Illinois authorizes series LLCs under 805 ILCS 180/37-40; the articles of organization must authorize series, each series needs a certificate of designation ($50), and each series must keep separate records and assets, with the operating agreement providing for the series.
illinois.foreign_llc: A foreign LLC must file an application for admission with the Illinois Secretary of State before transacting business in Illinois; $150 (805 ILCS 180/50-10)
illinois.single_member: One member is enough to form an Illinois LLC, and a sole member can have an operating agreement (805 ILCS 180/1-5).

indiana.overview: Indiana LLCs file Articles of Organization (State Form 49459) with the Secretary of State, Business Services Division, through the INBiz portal. Indiana has no annual report and no franchise tax; instead LLCs file a Business Entity Report only every two years. Indiana also authorizes series LLCs.
indiana.filing_office: Indiana Secretary of State, Business Services Division
indiana.registered_agent: The LLC must have a registered agent in Indiana, either an Indiana resident individual or an entity authorized in Indiana, with an Indiana street address.
indiana.operating_agreement: recommended, not required (Ind. Code section 23-18-4-4; not filed with the state)
indiana.annual_report: No annual report; a Business Entity Report is due every two years in the LLC's formation anniversary month; $32 online / $50 by mail
indiana.series_llc: Yes — Indiana authorizes series LLCs under Ind. Code Title 23, Article 18.1; a master LLC's articles of organization must authorize series, the master LLC must have an operating agreement, and each series can have separate rights, assets and liabilities if records and accounts are kept separate.
indiana.foreign_llc: A foreign LLC must file a Foreign Registration Statement with the Indiana Secretary of State through INBiz before transacting business in Indiana. A foreign LLC must file a Foreign Registration Statement with the Indiana Secretary of State through INBiz before transacting business in Indiana; the fee is $105 online / $125 on paper (State Form 56369).

iowa.overview: Iowa LLCs are formed by filing a Certificate of Organization with the Secretary of State for $50. Unusually, Iowa publishes no fill-in form for the certificate; the filer drafts it to the requirements of Iowa Code section 489.201 and uploads it through Fast Track Filing. Iowa has no annual report, only a biennial report in odd-numbered years.
iowa.filing_office: Iowa Secretary of State, Business Services Division
iowa.registered_agent: The LLC must designate and maintain a registered agent with a place of business in Iowa, with an Iowa street address and mailing address (Iowa Code section 489.115).
iowa.operating_agreement: recommended, not required (Iowa Code sections 489.102 and 489.105; the agreement may be oral, implied or written and is not filed with the Secretary of State)
iowa.annual_report: No annual report; a biennial report is due January 1 to April 1 of each odd-numbered year, starting the first odd-numbered year after formation; $30 online / $45 on paper
iowa.series_llc: Yes — Iowa authorizes protected series under Iowa Code chapter 489, subchapter XIV, sections 489.14101 et seq. (Uniform Protected Series Act); each protected series is treated as a separate LLC with its own assets and liabilities.
iowa.foreign_llc: A foreign LLC must file an application for a certificate of registration with the Iowa Secretary of State before transacting business in Iowa; $100 (Iowa Code section 489.122)
iowa.single_member: One person can form an Iowa LLC, and a sole member's operating agreement is recognized under Iowa law.

kansas.overview: Kansas LLCs file Articles of Organization (Form DL) with the Secretary of State for $85 online, after a fee cut effective February 27, 2026. Kansas has no annual report; LLCs file a Business Entity Information Report every two years. Kansas also authorizes series LLCs.
kansas.registered_agent: The LLC must have a resident agent in Kansas, a Kansas resident individual or an entity authorized in Kansas, with a Kansas street address (a P.O. box is not accepted), available during business hours (K.S.A. 17-7925).
kansas.operating_agreement: recommended, not required (K.S.A. 17-7663 defines an operating agreement as written, oral or implied; it is not filed with the Secretary of State)
kansas.annual_report: No annual report; a Business Entity Information Report is due every two years by April 15 of the reporting year, based on whether the LLC formed in an even or odd year; $90 online / $110 on paper
kansas.series_llc: Yes — Kansas authorizes series LLCs under K.S.A. 17-76,143; file Articles of Organization for an LLC that may create series (Form LAO), and the operating agreement may establish one or more designated series with separate rights, powers and duties.
kansas.foreign_llc: A foreign LLC must register with the Kansas Secretary of State before transacting business in Kansas. A foreign LLC must register with the Kansas Secretary of State before transacting business in Kansas; the fee is $115 (Application for Registration, Form FA).

kentucky.overview: Kentucky has one of the lowest LLC filing fees in the country at $40, filed with the Secretary of State, Division of Business Filings. A copy of the Articles of Organization must also be filed with the county clerk where the registered office is located. Kentucky LLCs also owe a Limited Liability Entity Tax with a $175 minimum each year.
kentucky.filing_office: Kentucky Secretary of State, Division of Business Filings
kentucky.registered_agent: The LLC must have a registered agent and a registered office in Kentucky, with a Kentucky street address; a copy of the Articles of Organization must also be filed with the county clerk of the county where the registered office is located (KRS 14A.2-040).
kentucky.operating_agreement: recommended, not required (KRS 275.015(21) defines an operating agreement as written or oral; it is not filed with the state)
kentucky.annual_report: Annual report due each year between January 1 and June 30, starting the year after formation; $15
kentucky.foreign_llc: A foreign LLC must file an Application for Certificate of Authority with the Kentucky Secretary of State before transacting business in Kentucky; $90
kentucky.single_member: One member is enough to form a Kentucky LLC.

louisiana.overview: Louisiana LLCs file Articles of Organization (Form 365) with the Secretary of State, Commercial Division, together with a required Initial Report (Form 973). The fee rose from $100 to $125 on October 1, 2026 under Act 921. Online filing through geauxBIZ is required in 14 parishes, and online filers are prompted for an EIN because formation and tax registration run together.
louisiana.filing_fee: $125 (covers the Articles of Organization and the Initial Report filed together; rose from $100 on October 1, 2026 under Act 921)
louisiana.filing_office: Louisiana Secretary of State, Commercial Division
louisiana.registered_agent: The LLC must have a registered agent with a physical Louisiana street address (a P.O. box alone is not enough), and the agent must sign an acceptance on the Initial Report.
louisiana.operating_agreement: recommended, not required (La. R.S. 12:1301(A)(16) defines the operating agreement as written or oral for multi-member LLCs; a single-member LLC's agreement must be written; a written agreement must be kept at the registered office under La. R.S. 12:1319)
louisiana.annual_report: Annual report due each year on or before the anniversary of the LLC's organization; $35
louisiana.foreign_llc: A foreign LLC must file an application for authority to transact business with the Louisiana Secretary of State; $185 (since October 1, 2026 under Act 921)
louisiana.single_member: A single-member LLC's operating agreement must be in writing (La. R.S. 12:1301(A)(16)).

maine.overview: Maine LLCs file a Certificate of Formation (Form MLLC-6) with the Secretary of State, Division of Corporations, UCC and Commissions, for $175. Formation is by mail or in person only; there is no online filing for forming an LLC. Maine is unusual in requiring that an LLC agreement exist, even though it is never filed with the state.
maine.filing_office: Maine Secretary of State, Division of Corporations, UCC and Commissions
maine.registered_agent: The LLC must have a registered agent, either a commercial or noncommercial registered agent, with a physical Maine street address (P.O. boxes are not accepted).
maine.operating_agreement: required — a limited liability company agreement must exist before, at or after filing (31 MRSA section 1531), but it is not filed with the state and may be written, oral or implied (31 MRSA section 1502)
maine.annual_report: Annual report due each year between January 1 and June 1, starting the year after formation; $85 for a domestic LLC
maine.foreign_llc: A foreign LLC must file a Statement of Foreign Qualification (Form MLLC-12) with the Maine Secretary of State before conducting activities in Maine; $250

maryland.overview: Maryland LLCs file Articles of Organization with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT), not the Secretary of State, for $100. The filing fee is modest but the ongoing cost is high: every LLC pays a $300 annual report fee each year. Standard review can take 6 to 8 weeks unless expedited review is paid for.
maryland.filing_office: Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
maryland.registered_agent: The LLC must have a resident agent who is a Maryland resident individual, a Maryland corporation, LLC or limited partnership, with a Maryland street address (not a P.O. box) (Md. Code, Corporations and Associations sections 1-101(x) and 4A-210).
maryland.operating_agreement: recommended, not required (Md. Code, Corporations and Associations section 4A-402: members may enter into an operating agreement and it need not be in writing unless the articles of organization require it; not filed with the state)
maryland.annual_report: Annual Report and Personal Property Return (Form 1) due each year by April 15, starting the year after formation; $300
maryland.series_llc: No — Maryland law does not authorize domestic series LLCs; foreign series companies formed under another state's series statute may register to do business in Maryland.
maryland.foreign_llc: A foreign LLC must register with SDAT before transacting business in Maryland; $100 (Md. Code, Corporations and Associations section 4A-1001)
maryland.single_member: One member is enough to form a Maryland LLC, and the statute expressly accepts a one-member operating agreement (Md. Code, Corporations and Associations section 4A-402).

massachusetts.overview: Massachusetts has the most expensive LLC costs in the country: $500 to form and $500 every year for the annual report. You file a Certificate of Organization with the Secretary of the Commonwealth, and the LLC only legally exists once the state approves it. Every LLC must have a resident agent with a Massachusetts street address.
massachusetts.filing_office: Massachusetts Secretary of the Commonwealth — Corporations Division
massachusetts.registered_agent: Every LLC must have a resident agent with a street address in Massachusetts who can accept legal papers for the LLC; the agent can be a member, a manager, or a commercial agent service.
massachusetts.operating_agreement: recommended, not required — M.G.L. c. 156C does not require an operating agreement, but the state lists creating one as a formation step
massachusetts.annual_report: Annual report due each year on the anniversary of the original filing; $500
massachusetts.series_llc: No — state law does not authorize series LLCs; M.G.L. c. 156C contains no series provisions
massachusetts.foreign_llc: An out-of-state LLC must file a Foreign Limited Liability Company Application for Registration (M.G.L. c. 156C, sec. 48) with the Secretary of the Commonwealth; $500, plus a $500 annual report each year
massachusetts.single_member: A single-member LLC is taxed as a sole proprietorship by default and must get an EIN from the IRS if it meets IRS criteria, such as having employees

michigan.overview: Michigan is one of the cheapest states to form an LLC: $50 to file Articles of Organization (Form CSCL/CD-700) with the Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs (LARA), and a $25 annual statement due every February 15. Michigan charges no franchise tax on LLCs. Online filing runs through the MiBusiness Registry portal.
michigan.filing_office: Michigan Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs (LARA) — Corporations, Securities and Commercial Licensing Bureau, Corporations Division
michigan.registered_agent: Every LLC must have a resident agent and a registered office with a street address in Michigan; the agent can be a member, a manager, or a commercial registered agent service.
michigan.operating_agreement: recommended, not required — the Michigan LLC Act defines an operating agreement (MCL 450.4102) but does not require one; to count as an operating agreement under Michigan law it must be in writing
michigan.annual_report: Annual statement due February 15 each year; $25 for an LLC ($75 for a professional LLC, with a $50 late fee after February 15)
michigan.series_llc: No — state law does not authorize series LLCs; the Michigan Limited Liability Company Act (MCL 450.4101 et seq.) contains no series provisions
michigan.foreign_llc: An out-of-state LLC must file an Application for Certificate of Authority to Transact Business in Michigan with LARA; $50
michigan.single_member: A single-member LLC is permitted; its operating agreement must be in writing to qualify as an operating agreement under MCL 450.4102

minnesota.overview: Minnesota LLCs file Articles of Organization under Chapter 322C with the Secretary of State. The fee is $135 by mail or $155 online or in person, which counts as expedited service. There is no fee for the yearly annual renewal, but it must still be filed every year by December 31 or the LLC is administratively terminated.
minnesota.filing_fee: $155 online or in person / $135 by mail
minnesota.filing_office: Minnesota Secretary of State — Business Services
minnesota.registered_agent: Every LLC must continuously maintain a registered office in Minnesota and a registered agent at that office to accept legal papers (Minn. Stat. sec. 322C.0113); the agent can be a member or a commercial agent.
minnesota.operating_agreement: recommended, not required — Minn. Stat. ch. 322C does not require an operating agreement
minnesota.annual_report: Annual renewal due December 31 each year; $0 — free to file, but missing it triggers administrative termination with no grace period
minnesota.series_llc: No — state law does not authorize series LLCs; Minn. Stat. ch. 322C contains no series provisions and Minnesota has not enacted the Uniform Protected Series Act
minnesota.foreign_llc: An out-of-state LLC must file a Certificate of Authority before transacting business in Minnesota (Minn. Stat. sec. 322C.0803); $185 by mail / $205 online or in person

mississippi.overview: Mississippi charges only $50 to form an LLC and the yearly annual report is free. Filings are made online through the Secretary of State's Corporations portal. Every LLC must have a registered agent with a Mississippi street address.
mississippi.filing_office: Mississippi Secretary of State — Business Services Division
mississippi.registered_agent: Every LLC must appoint and maintain a registered agent with a street address in Mississippi under the Mississippi Registered Agents Act (Miss. Code Ann. sec. 79-35-5); the agent can be a member or a commercial agent.
mississippi.operating_agreement: recommended, not required — Mississippi law allows an LLC to be formed and operated without one; Miss. Code Ann. sec. 79-29-123 recognizes operating agreements as binding between members
mississippi.annual_report: Annual report due April 15 each year; $0 for a domestic LLC (foreign LLCs pay $250)
mississippi.series_llc: No — state law does not authorize series LLCs; the Revised Mississippi Limited Liability Company Act (Miss. Code Ann. secs. 79-29-101 to 79-29-1317) contains no series provisions
mississippi.foreign_llc: An out-of-state LLC must file an Application for Registration of Foreign LLC; $250, plus a $250 annual report each year

missouri.overview: Missouri charges $50 to file Articles of Organization online or $105 on paper, and Missouri LLCs file no annual report at all. Missouri is one of the few states whose statute says members shall adopt an operating agreement, and it authorizes series LLCs. The fee gap between the statute and the SOS schedule is a $5 Technology Fund charge.
missouri.filing_office: Missouri Secretary of State — Business Services Division (Corporations Division)
missouri.registered_agent: Every LLC must have a registered agent with a street address in Missouri to accept legal papers; the agent can be a member, a manager, or a commercial agent service.
missouri.operating_agreement: required — RSMo sec. 347.081.1 states the member or members shall adopt an operating agreement; a single-member LLC must have a written declaration (RSMo sec. 347.015(13))
missouri.annual_report: No annual report; $0 — Missouri LLCs file no annual or periodic report with the Secretary of State
missouri.series_llc: Yes — RSMo sec. 347.186 authorizes designated series of members, managers, or LLC interests; the articles of organization must separately identify each series and give notice of the liability limitation, and separate records must be kept for each series
missouri.foreign_llc: An out-of-state LLC must register on Form LLC-4, Application for Registration of a Foreign LLC; $105
missouri.single_member: A single-member LLC must adopt its operating agreement as a written declaration, since RSMo sec. 347.015(13) does not recognize an oral agreement with only one member

montana.overview: Montana has the lowest LLC formation fee in the country at $35, filed online only through the Secretary of State's Business Filing Portal. The annual report is normally $20 due April 15, but the state has waived the on-time fee for 2026 and 2027. Montana authorizes series LLCs.
montana.filing_fee: $35 (plus $50 for each series member named in a series LLC)
montana.filing_office: Montana Secretary of State — Business Services Division
montana.registered_agent: Every LLC must have a registered agent with a street address in Montana to accept legal papers (MCA sec. 35-7-105); the agent can be a member or a commercial agent.
montana.operating_agreement: recommended, not required — the Montana LLC Act does not require an operating agreement, but a series LLC must include the operating agreement of each series in its articles of organization (MCA sec. 35-8-202)
montana.annual_report: Annual report due April 15 each year; $20 normally, but $0 for on-time filings under the state's fee waiver for 2026 and 2027
montana.series_llc: Yes — MCA sec. 35-8-202 and sec. 35-8-304 authorize series of members; the articles must name each series, state whether a series debts are enforceable against that series assets only, and set out each series relative rights, and the filing fee adds $50 for each series member named
montana.foreign_llc: An out-of-state LLC must file a Certificate of Authority; $70 (plus $50 for each series member named)

nebraska.overview: Nebraska is one of only three states that require a new LLC to publish a notice of its formation in a newspaper for three straight weeks, then file proof of publication with the Secretary of State. The Certificate of Organization costs $100 online or $110 on paper, and LLCs file a biennial report every two years instead of an annual one.
nebraska.filing_fee: $100 online / $110 in office or by mail
nebraska.filing_office: Nebraska Secretary of State — Business Services Division
nebraska.registered_agent: Every LLC must have a registered agent for service of process with a street address in Nebraska (Neb. Rev. Stat. sec. 21-117); the agent can be a member or a commercial agent.
nebraska.operating_agreement: recommended, not required — the Nebraska Uniform Limited Liability Company Act does not require an operating agreement
nebraska.annual_report: Biennial report due January 1 to April 1 of each odd-numbered year; $25 online / $30 on paper (Neb. Rev. Stat. sec. 21-125)
nebraska.series_llc: Yes — the Nebraska Uniform Protected Series Act (Neb. Rev. Stat. secs. 21-501 to 21-542) authorizes protected series; each protected series is a distinct person, created by a filed designation costing $100 electronically or $110 in writing per series
nebraska.foreign_llc: An out-of-state LLC must file a Certificate of Authority; $100 online / $110 in writing

nevada.overview: Nevada's headline $75 articles fee is only part of the cost: formation also requires a $150 Initial List of Managers or Members and a $200 State Business License filed at the same time, for $425 total. Nevada has no state income tax and authorizes series LLCs. Filings go through the Secretary of State's online portal, now called ORION.
nevada.filing_fee: $75 for the Articles of Organization (total $425 at formation including the $150 Initial List and $200 State Business License, all filed together)
nevada.filing_office: Nevada Secretary of State — Commercial Recordings Division
nevada.registered_agent: Every LLC must have a registered agent with a physical street address in Nevada who is available during business hours (NRS 77.310 and NRS 86.161); the agent can be a member or a commercial agent, and the agent must file a certificate of acceptance.
nevada.operating_agreement: recommended, not required — NRS 86.286 permits an operating agreement but does not require one
nevada.annual_report: Annual List of Managers or Members ($150) plus State Business License renewal ($200), $350 total, due each year by the last day of the formation anniversary month
nevada.series_llc: Yes — NRS 86.296 authorizes series of members; each series can own property, contract, and sue or be sued in its own name, and a series debts are enforceable only against that series assets if separate records are kept and the articles or operating agreement so provide
nevada.foreign_llc: An out-of-state LLC must register as a foreign LLC; $75 for registration (NRS 86.561), plus the $150 list and $200 business license

new-hampshire.overview: New Hampshire charges $100 to file a Certificate of Formation (Form LLC-1) with the Corporation Division, or $102 online with the $2 electronic handling charge. Every LLC files a $100 annual report due April 1. New Hampshire has no individual income tax.
new-hampshire.filing_fee: $100 by mail / $102 online (includes a $2 electronic handling charge)
new-hampshire.filing_office: New Hampshire Secretary of State (Department of State) — Corporation Division
new-hampshire.registered_agent: Every LLC must designate and continuously maintain a registered agent with a street address in New Hampshire (RSA 304-C:36); the agent must be a New Hampshire resident or an entity authorized to do business in New Hampshire, and must consent to the appointment.
new-hampshire.operating_agreement: recommended, not required — RSA chapter 304-C does not require an operating agreement
new-hampshire.annual_report: Annual report due April 1 each year; $100 ($102 if filed online)
new-hampshire.series_llc: No — state law does not authorize series LLCs; RSA chapter 304-C contains no series provisions
new-hampshire.foreign_llc: An out-of-state LLC must file an Application for Registration as a Foreign LLC with the Corporation Division

new-jersey.overview: New Jersey LLCs file a Certificate of Formation with the Division of Revenue and Enterprise Services (DORES) in the Department of the Treasury, not the Secretary of State. The fee was cut from $125 to $100 effective July 1, 2026, and the annual report is $75 due in the LLC's formation anniversary month.
new-jersey.filing_office: New Jersey Department of the Treasury — Division of Revenue and Enterprise Services (DORES)
new-jersey.registered_agent: Every LLC must have a registered agent with a street address in New Jersey to accept legal papers (N.J.S.A. 42:2C-14); the agent can be a member or a commercial agent.
new-jersey.operating_agreement: recommended, not required — the New Jersey Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act does not require an operating agreement
new-jersey.annual_report: Annual report due each year by the last day of the LLC's formation anniversary month; $75
new-jersey.series_llc: No — state law does not authorize series LLCs; N.J.S.A. 42:2C-1 et seq. contains no series provisions
new-jersey.foreign_llc: An out-of-state LLC must file an Application for a Certificate of Authority; $100 (N.J.S.A. 42:2C-93, as amended by P.L. 2026, c.24)

new-mexico.overview: New Mexico has one of the cheapest and simplest LLC setups in the country: a $50 online-only filing and no annual report or recurring Secretary of State fee afterward. All business filings are handled online through the Secretary of State's SOS Enterprise portal, and paper filings are no longer accepted. The articles do not list member names, which gives New Mexico LLCs a degree of privacy.
new-mexico.filing_office: New Mexico Secretary of State, Business Services Division
new-mexico.registered_agent: Every LLC must continuously maintain a registered office and a registered agent in New Mexico (NMSA 1978, Section 53-19-5). The agent may be an individual resident of New Mexico, a New Mexico corporation, LLC or partnership, or a foreign entity authorized to do business in New Mexico.
new-mexico.operating_agreement: recommended, not required - New Mexico law does not require an operating agreement and it is not filed with the Secretary of State
new-mexico.annual_report: No annual report; $0 - New Mexico law requires no annual or biennial report and charges no recurring Secretary of State fee
new-mexico.foreign_llc: An out-of-state LLC must register with the Secretary of State by filing an Application for Registration with a certificate of good standing from its home state dated within 30 days; fee $100 (NMSA 1978, Section 53-19-63)
new-mexico.single_member: Single-member LLCs are allowed and follow the same formation steps as multi-member LLCs; the articles state whether the LLC is single-member or multi-member, and a single-member LLC needs an EIN only if it has employees or elects corporate tax treatment

new-york.overview: New York is one of the most expensive and demanding states for LLC formation: the $200 filing fee is only the start, because most LLCs must also publish a formation notice in two county newspapers for six weeks and file a Certificate of Publication. The Secretary of State is the statutory agent for service of process for every LLC, so a separate registered agent is optional. New York is also one of the few states that requires a written operating agreement.
new-york.filing_office: New York Department of State, Division of Corporations
new-york.registered_agent: The Secretary of State is the statutory agent for service of process for every New York LLC under LLC Law Section 301, and the LLC must designate an address where process is mailed; hiring a separate commercial registered agent is optional, not required
new-york.operating_agreement: required - members shall adopt a written operating agreement under LLC Law Section 417, before, at the time of, or within 90 days after filing the Articles of Organization; it is an internal document and is not filed with the Department of State
new-york.annual_report: Biennial Statement due every two years in the calendar month the Articles of Organization were filed; $9. LLCs also owe a separate annual filing fee to the Department of Taxation and Finance based on New York source gross income, starting at $25
new-york.series_llc: No - state law does not authorize series LLCs
new-york.foreign_llc: An out-of-state LLC must file an Application for Authority under LLC Law Section 802; fee $250, and the publication requirement also applies to foreign LLCs
new-york.single_member: Single-member LLCs are allowed; an LLC may be formed by one or more persons, and the same $200 fee, publication requirement and operating agreement rule apply

north-carolina.overview: North Carolina charges a moderate $125 to form an LLC, but its $200 annual report is one of the highest recurring LLC fees in the country, so the long-term cost matters more than the formation fee. Articles of Organization (Form L-01) are filed with the Secretary of State, Business Registration Division, online or by mail. The annual report is due every April 15 starting the year after formation.
north-carolina.filing_fee: $125 online or by mail (online card payments add a $3 electronic fee, $2 by ACH)
north-carolina.filing_office: North Carolina Secretary of State, Business Registration Division
north-carolina.registered_agent: Every LLC must continuously maintain a registered agent with a physical street address in North Carolina; a P.O. box does not qualify. The agent may be an individual North Carolina resident or a domestic or foreign entity authorized to do business in North Carolina, and must be available during business hours
north-carolina.operating_agreement: recommended, not required - North Carolina does not require an operating agreement; where there is none, the default rules of N.C.G.S. Chapter 57D, Section 57D-2-30 apply
north-carolina.annual_report: Annual report due April 15 each year, starting the year after the year of formation; $200 on paper, $203 online by card or $202 by ACH
north-carolina.series_llc: No - state law does not authorize series LLCs
north-carolina.foreign_llc: An out-of-state LLC must file an Application for Certificate of Authority with a certificate of existence from its home state issued within 6 months; fee $250, and foreign LLCs file the same April 15 annual report

north-dakota.overview: North Dakota forms LLCs entirely through the Secretary of State's FirstStop online portal, with a $135 filing fee and a $50 annual report due each November 15. The articles name only the organizers and the registered agent, not the members. North Dakota offers business, farm and ranch, nonprofit and professional LLC types, all at the same $135 fee.
north-dakota.filing_office: North Dakota Secretary of State, Business Services
north-dakota.registered_agent: Every LLC must maintain a registered agent with a physical street address in North Dakota; a P.O. box does not qualify. The agent may be a commercial registered agent on the state's list or a noncommercial agent such as a North Dakota resident individual, and the LLC itself may not serve as its own registered agent
north-dakota.operating_agreement: recommended, not required - North Dakota law does not require a written operating agreement (N.D.C.C. Section 10-32.1-13); an operating agreement may be oral, written, implied or a combination (N.D.C.C. Section 10-32.1-02(36)) and is not filed with the state
north-dakota.annual_report: Annual report due by November 15 each year, starting the year after formation; $50, plus a $50 late fee if filed after the deadline. Farm, ranch and authorized livestock farm LLCs file by April 15 instead
north-dakota.series_llc: Yes - North Dakota law provides for series LLCs under N.D.C.C. Chapter 10-32.1, with separate assets and liabilities for each series when separate records are kept
north-dakota.foreign_llc: An out-of-state LLC must obtain a certificate of authority from the Secretary of State before transacting business in North Dakota; fee $135, the same as a domestic LLC

ohio.overview: Ohio is a low-cost, low-maintenance state for LLCs: a $99 filing fee and no annual report or recurring state fee afterward. LLCs file Articles of Organization (Form 610) with the Secretary of State online through Ohio Business Central or by mail. Ohio calls the registered agent a statutory agent, and the agent's signed acceptance must accompany the filing.
ohio.registered_agent: Every LLC must appoint a statutory agent before filing, under Ohio Rev. Code Section 1706.09. The agent must be an Ohio resident individual or an entity with a business address in Ohio, with a physical street address (a P.O. box alone does not qualify), and the agent's signed acceptance is filed with the articles
ohio.operating_agreement: recommended, not required - Ohio does not require an operating agreement and it is not filed with the state; Ohio law recognizes written, oral or implied agreements
ohio.annual_report: No annual report; $0 - Ohio does not require LLCs to file an annual report or pay a yearly state fee
ohio.series_llc: Yes - Ohio law permits series LLCs under Ohio Rev. Code Chapter 1706; the articles must include a series statement, and each series has separate assets and liabilities if records are kept separate
ohio.foreign_llc: An out-of-state LLC registers by filing a Registration of a Foreign Limited Liability Company (Form 617) with the Secretary of State; fee $99
ohio.single_member: Single-member LLCs are allowed; Ohio permits an LLC with just one owner, and the same $99 filing and statutory agent rules apply

oklahoma.overview: Oklahoma is one of the cheapest states to run an LLC: a $100 formation fee and a $25 Annual Certificate each year, with no franchise tax on LLCs. Articles of Organization (Form 0073) are filed with the Secretary of State online, by mail or in person. Oklahoma also authorizes registered series LLCs, which are uncommon.
oklahoma.filing_fee: $100 online, by mail or in person (online card payments add about a 4% service charge, about $104 total)
oklahoma.filing_office: Oklahoma Secretary of State, Business Filing Department
oklahoma.registered_agent: Every LLC must continuously maintain a registered office in Oklahoma and a registered agent under 18 O.S. Section 2010. The agent may be the LLC itself, an individual Oklahoma resident, or a domestic or qualified foreign corporation, LLC or partnership, with a street address (not a P.O. box) and a business office open during regular business hours
oklahoma.operating_agreement: recommended, not required - Oklahoma law defines an operating agreement as any agreement of the members, including a sole member, whether oral, in a record, implied or a combination (18 O.S. Section 2001(16)); it is not filed with the Secretary of State
oklahoma.annual_report: Annual Certificate due each year on the anniversary date of the filing of the Articles of Organization; $25, with a 60-day grace period before the LLC loses good standing
oklahoma.series_llc: Yes - Oklahoma law authorizes registered series LLCs; each series is registered with the Secretary of State and the filing fee for a registered series LLC is $100
oklahoma.foreign_llc: An out-of-state LLC files a Registration of Foreign Limited Liability Company with the Secretary of State; fee $300

oregon.overview: Oregon charges $100 to form an LLC and the same $100 every year to renew, so formation and upkeep cost exactly the same. Articles of Organization are filed with the Secretary of State, Corporation Division, through the Oregon Business Registry online or by mail. The annual report (renewal) is due each year on the anniversary of the original filing.
oregon.filing_office: Oregon Secretary of State, Corporation Division (Business Registry)
oregon.registered_agent: Every LLC must appoint and keep a registered agent with a physical street address in Oregon; a P.O. box does not qualify. The agent must be an Oregon resident or an Oregon or authorized foreign business entity, and must be available during regular business hours (ORS 63.111)
oregon.operating_agreement: recommended, not required - Oregon does not require an operating agreement and it is not filed with the state; without one, the default rules of ORS Chapter 63 apply (ORS 63.057)
oregon.annual_report: Annual report (renewal) due each year on the anniversary date of the original filing; $100, filed online through the Oregon Business Registry
oregon.series_llc: No - state law does not authorize series LLCs
oregon.foreign_llc: An out-of-state LLC must file an Application for Authority to Transact Business with the Secretary of State, with a certificate of existence from its home state dated within 60 days; fee $275, and the foreign annual renewal is also $275

pennsylvania.overview: Pennsylvania forms LLCs with a Certificate of Organization (Form DSCB:15-8821) plus a docketing statement, for $125, and is very cheap to maintain afterward thanks to a $7 annual report. Pennsylvania does not use the term registered agent: LLCs name a registered office instead. Since 2025 every LLC files a $7 annual report by September 30, replacing the old once-a-decade report.
pennsylvania.filing_office: Pennsylvania Department of State, Bureau of Corporations and Charitable Organizations
pennsylvania.registered_agent: Every LLC must have a registered office in Pennsylvania at a street address or rural route box number; a P.O. box alone is not acceptable. A separate registered agent is not required, and an LLC with no Pennsylvania address may instead name a Commercial Registered Office Provider (CROP) from the Department's list
pennsylvania.operating_agreement: recommended, not required - Pennsylvania does not require an operating agreement; an agreement may be oral, implied, in a record, or a combination, and it is not filed with the Department of State
pennsylvania.annual_report: Annual report (Form DSCB:15-146) due January 1 through September 30 each year, starting the year after formation; $7 for a for-profit LLC, no fee for a not-for-profit LLC. From reports due in 2027, a missed report can lead to administrative dissolution six months after the due date
pennsylvania.series_llc: No - state law does not authorize series LLCs
pennsylvania.foreign_llc: An out-of-state LLC must file a Foreign Registration Statement (Form DSCB:15-412) with a docketing statement (Form DSCB:15-134A) with the Department of State; fee $250, and foreign LLCs file the same $7 annual report

rhode-island.overview: Rhode Island costs more to keep than to form: the $150 filing fee is modest, but every LLC also owes a $400 annual minimum tax to the Division of Taxation whether or not it makes a profit, plus a $50 annual report. Articles of Organization (Form 400) are filed with the Department of State, Business Services Division, online, by mail or in person.
rhode-island.filing_fee: $150 online, by mail or in person
rhode-island.filing_office: Rhode Island Department of State, Business Services Division
rhode-island.registered_agent: Every LLC must have a resident agent for service of process in Rhode Island. The agent must be a Rhode Island resident or a Rhode Island or authorized foreign corporation, LLC or limited partnership, with an actual Rhode Island street address, available during normal business hours; a P.O. box is not accepted (R.I. Gen. Laws Section 7-16-11)
rhode-island.operating_agreement: recommended, not required - Rhode Island does not require an operating agreement and it is not filed with the state
rhode-island.annual_report: Annual Report for a Limited Liability Company (Form 632) due February 1 through May 1 each year, starting the year after formation; $50, plus a $2.50 enhanced access fee online and a $25 late penalty after June 1. Every LLC also owes a $400 minimum annual tax to the Division of Taxation, not prorated
rhode-island.foreign_llc: An out-of-state LLC registers by filing an Application for Registration for a Foreign Limited Liability Company (Form 450) with the Department of State; fee $150

south-carolina.overview: South Carolina is one of the simplest states for LLC upkeep: a $110 formation fee and, for most LLCs, no annual report and no recurring Secretary of State fee at all. Articles of Organization are filed with the Secretary of State online through Business Entities Online or by mail. Only LLCs that elect corporate tax treatment owe an annual report, and that goes to the Department of Revenue, not the Secretary of State.
south-carolina.filing_fee: $110 ($125 online including the $15 SC.gov service fee)
south-carolina.registered_agent: Every LLC must have an agent for service of process with a physical street address in South Carolina; a P.O. box does not qualify. The agent's name and address are listed on the Articles of Organization
south-carolina.operating_agreement: recommended, not required - South Carolina does not require an operating agreement and it is not filed with the Secretary of State
south-carolina.annual_report: No annual report for most LLCs; $0. An LLC taxed as a corporation files an annual report (CL-1) with the Department of Revenue, with a $25 license fee
south-carolina.foreign_llc: An out-of-state LLC registers by filing an Application for a Certificate of Authority by a Foreign Limited Liability Company (Form F0008) with a certificate of good standing from its home state; fee $110
south-carolina.single_member: Single-member LLCs are allowed; an LLC may be formed by a single owner or with partners, following the same filing steps

south-dakota.overview: South Dakota is a low-cost place to form an LLC, with a $150 online filing fee and online filings processed immediately. There is no state income tax, and the state authorizes series LLCs. The only routine recurring state cost is the annual report, $55 online.
south-dakota.filing_office: South Dakota Secretary of State — Business Services Division
south-dakota.registered_agent: Every LLC must continuously maintain a registered agent with a physical street address in South Dakota (not a P.O. box) who is available during normal business hours to accept legal papers; the agent may be a South Dakota resident or a business entity authorized to do business in the state.
south-dakota.annual_report: Annual report due each year by the last day of the anniversary month; $55 online / $70 by paper
south-dakota.series_llc: Yes — South Dakota authorizes series LLCs under SDCL 47-34A-202.1; articles of organization for a series LLC cost $200
south-dakota.foreign_llc: A foreign LLC must file a Certificate of Authority with the Secretary of State before transacting business in South Dakota; the fee is $750 online / $765 by paper
south-dakota.single_member: Single-member LLCs are allowed; members and managers do not have to be South Dakota residents

tennessee.overview: Tennessee charges by the member rather than a flat fee, so it is one of the pricier states for larger LLCs: $300 minimum for up to six members, rising by $50 per member to a $3,000 maximum. LLCs also owe a separate franchise and excise tax return to the Department of Revenue each year. After filing, a copy of the Articles of Organization must be recorded with the county Register of Deeds.
tennessee.filing_fee: $300 minimum (1-6 members); $50 per additional member over 6, up to $3,000
tennessee.filing_office: Tennessee Secretary of State — Division of Business and Charitable Organizations
tennessee.registered_agent: Every LLC must continuously maintain a registered agent with a physical street address in Tennessee (not a P.O. box) who is available during normal business hours to accept legal papers; the agent may be a Tennessee resident or a business entity authorized to do business in the state.
tennessee.annual_report: Annual report due each year on or before the first day of the fourth month after the fiscal year ends (April 1 for a calendar-year LLC); $300 minimum, $50 per member over six, up to $3,000
tennessee.series_llc: Yes — Tennessee authorizes series LLCs under Tenn. Code Ann. Title 48, Chapter 249, Part 9, at no extra formation fee
tennessee.foreign_llc: An LLC formed in another state must file an Application for Certificate of Authority with the Tennessee Secretary of State before transacting business in Tennessee and must maintain a Tennessee registered agent An LLC formed in another state must file an Application for Certificate of Authority with the Tennessee Secretary of State before transacting business in Tennessee and must maintain a Tennessee registered agent; the fee is $300 minimum ($50 per member, $300 to $3,000).
tennessee.single_member: Single-member LLCs are allowed; Tennessee also requires recording a copy of the Articles of Organization with the county Register of Deeds

texas.overview: Texas charges a flat $300 to file a Certificate of Formation (Form 205) with the Secretary of State, the same by every filing method. There is no annual report and no state income tax, but every LLC files a franchise tax report and Public Information Report with the Texas Comptroller each year. Texas also authorizes series LLCs.
texas.filing_office: Texas Secretary of State — Corporations Section
texas.registered_agent: Every LLC must continuously maintain a registered agent with a physical street address in Texas (not a P.O. box) who is available during normal business hours to accept legal papers; the agent may be a Texas resident or an entity authorized to do business in Texas (Tex. Bus. Orgs. Code Sec. 5.201)
texas.operating_agreement: recommended, not required (Tex. Bus. Orgs. Code Sec. 101.052)
texas.annual_report: No annual report with the Secretary of State; $0. Instead, file a franchise tax report and Public Information Report with the Texas Comptroller by May 15 each year; no franchise tax is due if annualized revenue is at or below the $2.65 million no-tax-due threshold (2026)
texas.series_llc: Yes — Texas authorizes series LLCs under Tex. Bus. Orgs. Code Chapter 101, Subchapter M; each series can hold separate assets and liabilities
texas.foreign_llc: A foreign LLC must register with the Texas Secretary of State before transacting business in Texas; the registration fee is $750
texas.single_member: Single-member LLCs are allowed; a single-member LLC is taxed as a disregarded entity by default for federal tax purposes

utah.overview: Utah is one of the cheapest states for LLCs: a $59 Certificate of Organization (Utah's name for the articles of organization) and an $18 annual renewal. Business filings go through the Department of Commerce, Division of Corporations and Commercial Code, not a Secretary of State, and most online filings are approved immediately. Utah also authorizes series LLCs through the operating agreement.
utah.filing_office: Utah Department of Commerce — Division of Corporations and Commercial Code
utah.registered_agent: Every LLC must continuously maintain a registered agent with a physical street address in Utah (not a P.O. box) who is available during normal business hours to accept legal papers; the agent may be a Utah resident or a business entity authorized to do business in the state
utah.annual_report: Annual renewal due each year in the anniversary month of formation; $18
utah.series_llc: Yes — Utah Code Sec. 48-3a-1201 authorizes designated series of transferable interests created by the operating agreement; no separate state filing per series, but the certificate of organization must include notice of the limitation on liability (Sec. 48-3a-1202)
utah.foreign_llc: A foreign LLC must file an Application for Registration with the Division of Corporations and Commercial Code before transacting business in Utah and must maintain a Utah registered agent A foreign LLC must file an Application for Registration with the Division of Corporations and Commercial Code before transacting business in Utah and must maintain a Utah registered agent; the fee is $59.

vermont.overview: Vermont charges $155 to file Articles of Organization, the same online or by mail, and online filings are normally processed in under one business day. Note the Secretary of State fee page may still show the older $125 figure; the $155 fee was set by statute (11 V.S.A. Sec. 4012, Act 77 of 2023). Vermont does not authorize series LLCs, but it does allow blockchain-based LLCs.
vermont.filing_office: Vermont Secretary of State — Business Services Division
vermont.registered_agent: Every LLC must designate and continuously maintain an agent for service of process with a physical street address in Vermont (not a P.O. box) who is available during normal business hours; the agent may be a Vermont resident or a business entity authorized to do business in the state (11 V.S.A. Sec. 4007)
vermont.annual_report: Annual report due each year within three months after the end of the LLC's fiscal year (March 31 for a calendar-year LLC); $45
vermont.series_llc: No — state law does not authorize series LLCs; Vermont has no series LLC statute under 11 V.S.A. Chapter 25, so each property or venture needs its own LLC
vermont.foreign_llc: A foreign LLC must obtain a certificate of authority from the Vermont Secretary of State before transacting business in Vermont and must maintain a Vermont agent for service of process A foreign LLC must obtain a certificate of authority from the Vermont Secretary of State before transacting business in Vermont and must maintain a Vermont agent for service of process; the fee is $155.
vermont.single_member: Single-member LLCs are allowed; Vermont also permits blockchain-based LLCs under 11 V.S.A. Sec. 4173

virginia.overview: Virginia has no Secretary of State for business filings; LLCs file with the State Corporation Commission (SCC) for a flat $100. Virginia files no annual report at all, charging instead a $50 annual registration fee. Virginia also authorizes series LLCs with protected series.
virginia.filing_office: Virginia State Corporation Commission — Office of the Clerk
virginia.registered_agent: Every LLC must continuously maintain a registered agent with a physical street address in Virginia (not a P.O. box) who is available during normal business hours to accept legal papers; the agent may be a Virginia resident or a business entity authorized to do business in Virginia (Va. Code Sec. 13.1-1015)
virginia.annual_report: No annual report; $0. Instead, a $50 annual registration fee is assessed by the SCC, due by the last day of the anniversary month each year after formation
virginia.series_llc: Yes — Virginia authorizes series LLCs with protected series under Va. Code Sec. 13.1-1088 et seq. (Article 16, Protected Series); each protected series is registered separately with the SCC
virginia.foreign_llc: A foreign LLC must obtain a certificate of registration from the State Corporation Commission before transacting business in Virginia; the fee is $100, the same as a domestic filing

washington.overview: Washington charges $200 to file a Certificate of Formation online ($180 by mail), plus a $10 Initial Report due within 120 days of formation. There is no state income tax, but LLCs pay business and occupation (B&O) tax on gross receipts and most need a separate business license from the Department of Revenue. Washington does not authorize series LLCs.
washington.filing_office: Washington Secretary of State — Corporations and Charities Division
washington.registered_agent: Every LLC must continuously maintain a registered agent with a physical street address in Washington (not a P.O. box) who is available during normal business hours to accept legal papers; the agent may be a Washington resident or a business entity authorized to do business in the state (RCW 23.95.415)
washington.annual_report: Annual report due each year by the last day of the anniversary month; $70. An Initial Report is also due within 120 days of formation ($10 if filed separately from the Certificate of Formation)
washington.series_llc: No — state law does not authorize series LLCs; Washington has not adopted series LLC legislation, and RCW 25.15 contains no series provisions
washington.foreign_llc: A foreign LLC must file a Foreign Registration Statement with the Secretary of State before transacting business in Washington; the fee is $200 online / $180 by mail, the same as a domestic filing
washington.single_member: Single-member LLCs are allowed; Washington courts may foreclose on a charging-order lien against a member's interest (RCW 25.15.252)

west-virginia.overview: West Virginia charges $100 to file Articles of Organization (Form LLD-1), with the initial fee waived for veteran-owned businesses and for West Virginia residents under 30. A separate $30 business registration certificate from the State Tax Department is also required. As of 2026, West Virginia authorizes protected series LLCs under a new law.
west-virginia.filing_fee: $100 by mail / $101 online (includes $1 portal processing fee)
west-virginia.filing_office: West Virginia Secretary of State — Business and Licensing Division
west-virginia.registered_agent: Every LLC must continuously maintain an agent for service of process with a physical street address in West Virginia (not a P.O. box) who is available during normal business hours to accept legal papers; the agent may be a West Virginia resident or a business entity authorized to do business in the state (W. Va. Code Sec. 31B-1-108)
west-virginia.annual_report: Annual report due each year between January 1 and June 30 (due July 1); $25, with a $50 late fee after July 1
west-virginia.series_llc: Yes — West Virginia adopted the Uniform Protected Series Act in 2026 (W. Va. Code Sec. 31B-14-101 et seq., effective June 12, 2026); a protected series is designated by filing Form LLD-11 with the Secretary of State for $25
west-virginia.foreign_llc: A foreign LLC must register with the West Virginia Secretary of State before transacting business in West Virginia; the fee is $150

wisconsin.overview: Wisconsin LLCs file with the Department of Financial Institutions, not the Secretary of State, and online filing costs $40 less than paper ($130 versus $170). The annual report is cheap at $25 online but has an unusual deadline: the end of the calendar quarter containing the formation anniversary. Full-time student entrepreneurs can have the formation fee waived.
wisconsin.filing_office: Wisconsin Department of Financial Institutions — Division of Corporate and Consumer Services
wisconsin.registered_agent: Every LLC must maintain a registered agent with a physical street address in Wisconsin (not a P.O. box or mailbox service) who is available during normal business hours to accept legal papers; the agent may be a Wisconsin resident or a business entity authorized to do business in the state (Wis. Stat. Sec. 183.0115). An LLC may not name itself as its own registered agent.
wisconsin.annual_report: Annual report due each year by the end of the calendar quarter containing the formation anniversary (March 31, June 30, September 30 or December 31), starting the year after formation; $25 online / $40 by paper
wisconsin.series_llc: Yes — Wisconsin law lets an operating agreement create designated series of members, managers, or LLC interests (Wis. Stat. sec. 183.0504), but Wisconsin law lacks a clear inter-series liability shield, so the protection is weaker than in some other series states — get local advice before relying on a series structure here.
wisconsin.foreign_llc: A foreign LLC must register with the Department of Financial Institutions before transacting business in Wisconsin; the fee is $100

wyoming.overview: Wyoming is a popular formation state: a flat $100 filing fee, no state income tax, no franchise tax, and member and manager names are not listed in public filings. It was the first state to authorize series LLCs. The annual report carries a license tax of at least $60 a year, based on Wyoming assets.
wyoming.filing_office: Wyoming Secretary of State — Business Division
wyoming.registered_agent: Every LLC must continuously maintain a registered agent with a physical street address in Wyoming (not a P.O. box) who is available during normal business hours to accept legal papers; the agent may be a Wyoming resident or a business entity authorized to do business in the state (Wyo. Stat. Sec. 17-28-103)
wyoming.annual_report: Annual report due each year on or before the first day of the anniversary month, starting the year after formation; license tax of $60 minimum or $0.0002 per dollar of Wyoming assets, whichever is greater
wyoming.series_llc: Yes — Wyoming was the first state to authorize series LLCs; Wyo. Stat. Sec. 17-29-211 allows an LLC to establish one or more series with separate assets and liabilities
wyoming.foreign_llc: A foreign LLC must file a Certificate of Authority with the Wyoming Secretary of State before transacting business in Wyoming and must maintain a Wyoming registered agent A foreign LLC must file a Certificate of Authority with the Wyoming Secretary of State before transacting business in Wyoming and must maintain a Wyoming registered agent; the fee is $150.
wyoming.single_member: Single-member LLCs are allowed; Wyoming does not list members or managers in public filings, and a creditor's sole remedy against a member's interest is a charging order (Wyo. Stat. Sec. 17-29-503)
